Figure 2:Teacher Drift in multilingual reasoning.(a)Student accuracy across languages.(b)Cumulative teacher-student likelihood ratioCi,tC_{i,t}indicates earlier alignment in low-resource languages.(c)Teacher recoverabilityRec⁡(m)\mathrm{Rec}(m)decreases with longer student prefixes.
Colors indicate language-resource groups.

Figure 3:Overview of TOPSD.The student generates a reasoning trajectory in the target language, while the privileged teacher additionally observes the English problem and reference solution.Step 1 (Teachable Prefix Selection)uses the cumulative teacher-student likelihood ratio to select a candidate teachable prefix, determiningwhereteacher supervision may be applied.Step 2 (Teacher Recoverability Verification)checks whether the teacher can recover the correct answer from the selected prefix, determiningwhethersupervision should be applied.
Only prefixes that pass verification receive distillation on the corresponding states of the original student trajectory.
English translations are shown in gray.
